solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See female cut in

indicators.note: something cut has had a bit trimmed off its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
to be in is to be at home, not out

explanation.surface: A woman is told to look at somebody who has pushed into a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is read as AT HOME, and 'cut' docks its last letter, leaving F + AT HOM = FATHOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it, just as 'I see' means I grasp the point.

clue.text: Numbers game

blocks.note: first meaning: plural of a digit, several of one particular figure
second meaning: a British court game where a ball is struck with the gloved hand

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a description of a maths puzzle, but it is two separate meanings; fives is a handball-like game played at some English schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a digit counts as numbers, and the same plural word names a traditional court ball sport.

clue.text: Take turns travelling in part of Central Asia

indicators.note: things travelling are on the move, so the letters move about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: Travellers on a long journey through Central Asia share the driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take turns' looks like an instruction to share, but it simply supplies the nine letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkestan is the historical region of Central Asia inhabited by Turkic peoples, now split among several countries.

clue.text: Overlook skinned cats

indicators.note: skinning strips away the outside, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: to cat is British slang for to be sick

explanation.surface: Someone ignores some cats that have been flayed, a grisly image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' is a verb here: in British slang to cat is to vomit, so VOMITS loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to leave it out or fail to include it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Liberal suffering decline

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
anguish is severe suffering

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's party is in decline and he is suffering for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' is the verb sense, to weaken or waste away.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to grow weak or fail to make progress, so it matches the verb meaning to weaken.

clue.text: Pictures of a couple surrounded by three kings

indicators.note: whatever is surrounded sits inside the other letters, which close round it

blocks.note: taken as written
R (rex) twice, and K for king as in chess notation
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A nativity painting of a couple, Mary and Joseph, surrounded by the three kings.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex gives R and chess notation gives K, so three kings can be split around the couple rather than kept together.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork means illustrations or pictorial material, so pictures collectively fits the word.

clue.text: Old bread pursued by fine bird, relative of pheasant

indicators.note: something pursued has others coming behind it, so the next pieces follow on

blocks.note: bread is slang for money, and the guinea is an old British coin
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Stale bread is chased by a handsome bird, game-bird cousin of the pheasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bread' is not stale loaves but old money: the guinea was a British gold coin worth 21 shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinea fowl are African game birds in the same order as pheasants, so they are related species.

clue.text: Feet — setter’s two to start with

blocks.note: the setter's is read as 'setter is', that is I AM
BI is the prefix meaning two, used at the start of words

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the setter has two feet to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's apostrophe-s stands for 'is', so the setter says I AM; 'two to start with' is the prefix BI-, as in bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi is the plural of iambus, a metrical foot of one short then one long syllable in poetry.

clue.text: Sycophants in hotel rile boy

blocks.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to rile someone is to anger them
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Fawning guests at a hotel irritate a young lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break falls in an unexpected place: the boy straddles the comma in the enumeration, so the pieces do not line up with the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on are toadies who attach themselves to someone for advantage, much as flattering sycophants do.

clue.text: Lazy ideas lacking any new energy

indicators.note: lacking any means having none at all, so every copy of a letter is dropped

blocks.note: notions are ideas
N is the abbreviation for new
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Idle thinking lacks fresh energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ns leave NOTIONS, giving OTIOS, and then E for energy is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose is an old word for idle or indolent, though it now more often means serving no purpose.

clue.text: Judgement of international court on cases of Verlaine and Rimbaud

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters of each word are used
in a down-free across reading, being on something means coming after it

blocks.note: first and last letters of the poet's name
first and last letters of the poet's name
I is the abbreviation for international
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: An international court rules on the cases of the poets Verlaine and Rimbaud, who famously quarrelled violently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' sounds legal, matching the court, but it means the outer letters; the court's I + CT is placed on after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the decision reached by a jury or court, so it is a formal judgement.

clue.text: Vitamin is first of many found in tahini spread

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only
something spread is spread about and rearranged, so the letters are scattered into a new order
being found in something means being inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
the letters used as written

explanation.surface: A health claim that tahini, the sesame paste, is the main source of a vitamin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tahini spread' suggests the paste on toast, but 'spread' tells you to rearrange its letters, with M placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, found in grains and seeds, so it is one of the named vitamins.

clue.text: Try drugs at last, I’m afraid

indicators.note: what comes at last is the final item, so the end letter is taken

blocks.note: final letter of the word
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: Someone finally tries drugs, adding nervously 'I'm afraid'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm afraid' looks like an apology but is a squeal of fear, EEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek to do something is to attempt it, so seek works as a verb for try.

clue.text: Make uniform and legwear to clothe Imogen head to toe

indicators.note: moving the head to the toe sends the first letter round to the end
clothing wraps around the body, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: hose are stockings or tights
the name as written

explanation.surface: School uniform and tights are provided to dress Imogen from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head to toe' sounds like dressing her completely, but it moves her first letter to the end of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: To homogenise is to make something consistent throughout, so the parts are all the same.

clue.text: Acerbic criminal nattering about closure of banks

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
about means around, so these letters go round another
a closure is an ending, so the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the letters used as written
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued crook chatters on about bank closures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the person, but it rearranges the letters, which then wrap around the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are harsh and biting, so the word is a synonym for sharply critical.

clue.text: Lush mountain enthralling mapmakers, you could say

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so these letters hold another piece inside

blocks.note: a lush is a drunkard, a sot
a peak is a mountain
OS is Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: A green mountain captivates surveyors, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like an adjective for the mountain but is the noun meaning drunkard, and the mapmakers sit between the drinker and the mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: So to speak is a phrase flagging a figurative expression, the same as saying 'you might put it that way'.

clue.text: Open to being led astray — rumpled bed is clue

indicators.note: rumpled means crumpled and messed up, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters used as written

explanation.surface: An unmade bed is the giveaway that someone succumbed to temptation.
explanation.walkthrough: The rumpled bed fits the seduction story, and its letters with IS CLUE make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seducible describes a person capable of being tempted or led astray, especially morally.

clue.text: We gather catchword wears thin

indicators.note: to gather is to learn by hearsay, so the word is taken as heard

blocks.note: a catchword is a popular phrase

explanation.surface: A popular slogan, we hear, has lost its force through overuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We gather' means we understand from hearsay; the phrase and the answer sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that frays becomes worn and ragged at the edges, so it is wearing thin.

clue.text: Poor accommodation of boy, timid little thing keeping quiet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: Al is a boy's name
a mouse is a small timid creature
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A shy little boy keeps quiet in his shabby lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor accommodation' sounds like substandard housing, but it means accommodation for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: An almshouse is a charitable house where poor or elderly people could live free.

clue.text: One giving Mafia boss gold

blocks.note: a don is a Mafia chief
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone hands gold over to a gangster chief.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, from French.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a person who gives money, blood or goods, so one giving describes them.

clue.text: Helps presidents to lose ego

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: chairwomen preside over meetings
the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: Advice that presidents should be less self-important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helps' is a noun: in Britain a daily help is a cleaner; ego is I, which drops out of CHAIRWOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Charwomen are cleaning ladies, and household cleaners are called helps in British usage.

clue.text: Heartless mentor managed rocker Eddie

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle has been taken out, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: a coach is a mentor or trainer
to run something is to manage it

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted mentor handled the career of a rock singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Cochran was the American rock and roll singer of 'Summertime Blues'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s American musician Eddie Cochran was a rock and roll star, so a rocker by that first name.

clue.text: Calm kid following lead of adventurer

indicators.note: the lead is what goes in front, so the opening letter is taken
following means coming after, so the first piece listed comes second

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A placid youngster trails behind an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is the verb, to tease, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at ease means relaxed and untroubled, so it is a phrase equivalent to calm.

clue.text: Made record of 100 poor children possessing nothing

indicators.note: to possess is to hold, so these letters hold another inside
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
the letters used as written
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone documented a hundred destitute children who owned nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes into CHILDREN and the whole lot is rearranged after C.
explanation.definitionFit: To chronicle events is to write a record of them in order, so the past tense means recorded.

clue.text: Mischievous libertine pinching prig’s backside

definitions.note: an adjective defining a word most often a noun; rogue is used attributively, and roguish would be stricter

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip tightly, so these letters close around another
the backside is the rear end, so the last letter is taken

blocks.note: a roué is a debauched man
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cheeky rake pinches the bottom of a prude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' and 'backside' play to the bottom-pinching picture; G goes inside ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a playful rascal, so the word carries the sense of mischievous, as in a rogue smile.

clue.text: Some exotic hummingbirds mate

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters are a portion of the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Certain tropical hummingbirds pair up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a verb about birds breeding, but it is the noun for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is a close friend, and mate is the British informal word for friend.

clue.text: Skinflint regularly emails heirs

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person keeps sending messages to his heirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a stingy person who hoards money, which is exactly a miser.

clue.text: Tragic queen made love

blocks.note: to make is to do, so made is did
love is zero in tennis scoring, O

explanation.surface: A doomed queen had a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made love' reads as one phrase, but splits into DID and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido, queen of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid, killed herself when Aeneas abandoned her.

clue.text: Dread of stomach lurgy coming to the fore

indicators.note: to come to the fore is to move to the front, so this piece goes first

blocks.note: lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness, a bug
to stomach something is to bear it

explanation.surface: Fear that a tummy bug is about to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like the body part but is the verb, to tolerate; the illness comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of fear or annoyance, so an object of dread.

clue.text: Students reviewed small mistakes

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: pupils are students
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Pupils looked again at their minor errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reviewed' suggests revision, but it turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip-ups are careless errors or blunders, which makes them mistakes in everyday speech.

clue.text: Stable having horse withdrawn from quality equestrian sport

indicators.note: withdrawn from means taken out of, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: stable means steady or even
a thing can be a characteristic or quality
horse is slang for heroin, H

explanation.surface: A racing stable has a horse scratched from a top-class riding event.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all horses, but 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventing is the horse-riding competition combining dressage, cross-country and show jumping.

clue.text: Charlatan in Post Office regrets returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A fraudster at the Post Office is sorry he came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts something inside, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur pretends to be something he is not, so like a charlatan he is a fake.
